item.title: French government in crisis talks after ‘colossal failure of the state’
item.description: Ministers, officials and police under pressure over response to days of violent unrest in cities across France The French government was in crisis talks on Sunday after one of the most violent days of unrest in years left public buildings burned, hundreds of shops destroyed and looted, and more than 2,000 people arrested in cities across the country . Politicians on the left and right called for the resignation of the interior minister, Laurent Nuñez, after the government appeared to have been caught by surprise by the scale of violence as state buildings were stormed and torched, bus stops… Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: Cost-of-living protests: Italian police clash with protesters in Milan, Bologna
item.description: Protests against inflation, low wages, and public service issues turned violent in multiple Italian cities. In Milan, protests erupted in Piazza Duomo where demonstrators clashed with police and vandalized property. Bologna saw similar unrest, with hooded youths attacking the central railway station and throwing projectiles at security forces. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni condemned the violence while supporting peaceful demonstrations. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

In part one, Simpson Cheung and Alfred Lam explore how the event could elevate the city’s status as an international financial centre at a pivotal moment. Beijing’s decision to have Hong Kong host the Apec Finance Ministers’ Meeting this week is a deliberate move to galvanise the city’s standing as an offshore renminbi... item.description: Dos hombres rastrearon los pasos del abogado y exjefe del ente recaudador de impuestos, una de las figuras más destacadas en la lucha contra la corrupción, y lo asesinaron en un campo de fútbol al que solía acudir los sábados para jugar.
